goal.problem: A pipeline stage failure after a 15-minute run forces a full restart from stage 1, wasting expensive Claude calls on stages 2-3 and crashing at stage 4 because the git branch already exists.
goal.solution: Add a --resume-from flag to run.py that skips completed stages using existing artifacts, and make executor.py check out an existing branch instead of failing.
goal.value: Pipeline operators recover from failures in seconds instead of re-running 15+ minutes of redundant Claude calls and manual branch cleanup.

components.name: Resume flag parser (run.py)
components.description: Extends argparse in run.py to accept --resume-from <stage_name>, validates it against the STAGES list, and skips stages before the specified one in the main loop.

components.name: Artifact prerequisite validator (run.py)
components.description: Before resuming, checks that all artifacts required by the resume stage exist on disk (e.g. resuming from executor requires pipeline/plans/<uuid>.json). Uses the existing artifacts dict and STAGES input-key mapping to determine which file must be present.

components.name: Resume command printer (run.py)
components.description: On any stage failure, prints the exact CLI command to resume from the failed stage (e.g. 'python pipeline/run.py pipeline/intake/<uuid>.json --resume-from executor') to stderr.

components.name: Branch collision handler (executor.py)
components.description: Replaces the current branch_exists check that calls sys.exit(1) with logic that checks out the existing pipeline/<uuid> branch instead of failing, enabling executor re-runs.

shape.integration_point: run.py main() CLI argument parsing and stage loop (lines 92-196); executor.py branch setup block (lines 265-280)
shape.pattern: Follows the existing STAGES list and artifacts dict pattern in run.py — each stage has a known input artifact key, so resume validation is a lookup into the same artifacts dict. Follows executor.py's existing branch_exists/create_branch helper pattern.
shape.data_flow: CLI --resume-from flag → stage name validated against STAGES list → artifact existence check using artifacts[stage_input_key] → stage loop skips stages before resume point → executor checks out existing branch if present → on failure, failed stage name → formatted resume command printed to stderr
shape.dependencies: Existing STAGES list and artifacts dict in run.py. Existing branch_exists() and git() helpers in executor.py. No new files or external dependencies.

behavior.input: run.py receives optional --resume-from <stage_name> CLI flag alongside the existing intake file path. Valid stage names: validate_intake, auto_refine, auto_plan, executor, auto_harden, approval.
processing: 1. run.py parses --resume-from argument and validates it is a known stage name from the STAGES list
2. run.py loads the intake JSON and extracts the UUID (existing logic, lines 101-129)
3. run.py builds the artifacts dict (existing logic, lines 132-139)
4. If --resume-from is set, run.py looks up the input artifact key for that stage from STAGES and checks the corresponding file exists in the artifacts dict
5. run.py iterates STAGES, skipping all stages before the --resume-from stage
6. Skipped stages are not executed but may be logged as skipped to stdout

7. For the executor stage specifically: executor.py checks branch_exists(f'pipeline/{uuid}'). If true, it runs git checkout pipeline/<uuid> instead of git checkout -b pipeline/<uuid>. If false, it creates the branch as before.
8. If any stage fails, run.py determines the failed stage name and prints to stderr: 'To resume: python pipeline/run.py <intake_path> --resume-from <failed_stage>'
behavior.output: Normal pipeline output (artifacts, board updates) for all stages that actually run. On failure: resume command string printed to stderr. On resume: skipped stages produce no artifacts or subprocess calls.

error_cases.trigger: --resume-from specifies an invalid stage name not in STAGES
error_cases.behavior: run.py prints 'Unknown stage: <name>. Valid stages: validate_intake, auto_refine, auto_plan, executor, auto_harden, approval' to stderr and exits with code 1

error_cases.trigger: --resume-from is set but the required input artifact for that stage does not exist on disk
error_cases.behavior: run.py prints 'Cannot resume from <stage>: missing prerequisite artifact <artifact_path>' to stderr and exits with code 1

error_cases.trigger: A stage fails during a normal (non-resume) run
error_cases.behavior: run.py prints the resume command to stderr after the existing failure output, then exits with code 1 as before

error_cases.trigger: A stage fails during a resumed run
error_cases.behavior: run.py prints the resume command for the failed stage to stderr, same as a normal failure

error_cases.trigger: executor.py encounters an existing branch pipeline/<uuid> during a resume
error_cases.behavior: executor.py prints 'Branch pipeline/<uuid> already exists, checking out' to stderr and runs git checkout pipeline/<uuid> instead of git checkout -b

edge_cases.behavior: Equivalent to a normal full run — no stages are skipped, artifact validation still runs (intake file must exist)
Skips stages 1-5, validates that pipeline/hardens/<uuid>.json exists, runs only the approval stage

edge_cases.condition: Artifact file exists but contains invalid JSON or has valid:false
edge_cases.behavior: Resume only checks file existence, not content validity. The resumed stage itself is responsible for validating its input as it already does today.

edge_cases.condition: executor.py runs without --resume-from and branch already exists
edge_cases.behavior: executor.py still checks out the existing branch instead of failing — the branch collision fix applies regardless of whether --resume-from was used

edge_cases.condition: validate_intake is the stage that fails (no prior artifacts to skip)
edge_cases.behavior: Resume command is still printed: '--resume-from validate_intake', which is equivalent to a full rerun

edge_cases.condition: Board.md status is already 'running' when resuming
edge_cases.behavior: Board status update on first-stage success only triggers if validate_intake ran. On resume from a later stage, board status is not re-updated to 'running' since it should already be set.

in_scope: Stage-skipping logic in run.py's main loop
Resume command output on any stage failure
Branch collision detection and checkout in executor.py

out_of_scope.reason: Resume is a manual recovery mechanism; automatic retry would require different failure classification logic and is a separate feature
Task scope is stage-level resume only; step-level resume inside executor would require tracking per-step completion state and is significantly more complex

out_of_scope.item: New files or new pipeline stages
out_of_scope.reason: Task explicitly scopes changes to run.py and executor.py modifications only
Each stage already validates its own input; duplicating that in the orchestrator adds coupling without benefit
Board updates are best-effort and silently skip failures already; resume does not change this contract

must_not_break: Normal (non-resume) pipeline runs must work identically to today
Stage ordering defined by the STAGES list must be preserved
UUID path-traversal validation in run.py must still run on resume
Executor's per-step retry logic (max_retries_per_step) must be unaffected
Executor's topological step ordering must be unaffected
Executor's commit-per-step pattern must be unaffected
Existing artifact file naming convention (pipeline/<dir>/<uuid>.json) must be unchanged
Exit codes: 0 for success, 1 for failure must be preserved

acceptance_criteria: Given a completed run with all artifacts present, when running 'python pipeline/run.py pipeline/intake/<uuid>.json --resume-from executor', then stages validate_intake, auto_refine, and auto_plan are not executed (no subprocesses spawned for them) and executor runs using pipeline/plans/<uuid>.json

Given --resume-from executor and pipeline/plans/<uuid>.json does not exist, when run.py starts, then it prints 'Cannot resume from executor: missing prerequisite artifact pipeline/plans/<uuid>.json' to stderr and exits with code 1 without running any stage

Given --resume-from nonexistent_stage, when run.py starts, then it prints 'Unknown stage: nonexistent_stage. Valid stages: validate_intake, auto_refine, auto_plan, executor, auto_harden, approval' to stderr and exits with code 1
Given a normal run where auto_plan fails, when run.py reports the failure, then it also prints 'To resume: python pipeline/run.py pipeline/intake/<uuid>.json --resume-from auto_plan' to stderr
Given a resumed run where auto_harden fails, when run.py reports the failure, then it prints 'To resume: python pipeline/run.py pipeline/intake/<uuid>.json --resume-from auto_harden' to stderr

Given branch pipeline/<uuid> already exists, when executor.py runs, then it checks out that branch (git checkout pipeline/<uuid>) instead of failing and prints 'Branch pipeline/<uuid> already exists, checking out' to stderr
Given branch pipeline/<uuid> does not exist, when executor.py runs, then it creates the branch with git checkout -b pipeline/<uuid> exactly as before
Given --resume-from validate_intake, when run.py starts, then all 6 stages run in order identically to a normal run
Given --resume-from approval and pipeline/hardens/<uuid>.json exists, when run.py starts, then only the approval stage runs
Given a normal run with no --resume-from flag, when run.py executes, then all stages run in order and no resume-related behavior changes the output

Given --resume-from executor and the artifact exists but contains invalid JSON, when run.py starts, then it does not reject the resume (file existence check passes) and the executor stage itself handles the validation error
Given executor.py encounters an existing branch during a non-resume normal run, when executor.py starts, then it checks out the existing branch instead of exiting with code 1

steps.description: Add --resume-from CLI flag parsing and validation to run.py
steps.code_spec:
In run.py main(), after the existing `intake_path = Path(sys.argv[1])` block but before the intake JSON reading, add argparse-based argument parsing. Specifically:

1. Replace the manual sys.argv parsing (lines 90-97) with argparse:
```python
import argparse  # add to imports at top
```

Replace:
```python
def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print("Usage: python pipeline/run.py <path_to_intake.json>", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    intake_path = Path(sys.argv[1])
    if not intake_path.exists():
        print(f"Intake file not found: {intake_path}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
```

With:
```python
def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Pipeline orchestrator")
    parser.add_argument("intake", help="Path to intake JSON file")
    parser.add_argument("--resume-from", dest="resume_from", default=None,
                        help="Resume from a specific stage (skip earlier stages)")
    cli_args = parser.parse_args()

    # Validate --resume-from against known stage names
    stage_names = [name for name, _, _ in STAGES]
    if cli_args.resume_from is not None and cli_args.resume_from not in stage_names:
        print(f"Unknown stage: {cli_args.resume_from}. Valid stages: {', '.join(stage_names)}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    intake_path = Path(cli_args.intake)
    if not intake_path.exists():
        print(f"Intake file not found: {intake_path}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
```

Store `resume_from = cli_args.resume_from` for use in later steps. Keep all existing logic after this point unchanged.

steps.description: Add artifact prerequisite validation when --resume-from is specified in run.py
steps.code_spec:
After the artifacts dict is built (line 139) and before the stage loop begins, add prerequisite validation. Insert this block:

```python
    resume_from = cli_args.resume_from

    # Validate prerequisite artifact exists when resuming
    if resume_from is not None:
        # Find the input_key for the resume stage
        resume_input_key = None
        for name, _, input_key in STAGES:
            if name == resume_from:
                resume_input_key = input_key
                break
        artifact_path = artifacts[resume_input_key]
        if not artifact_path.exists():
            print(f"Cannot resume from {resume_from}: missing prerequisite artifact {artifact_path}", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(1)
```

Place this after the `artifacts["intake"] = intake_path.resolve()` override (line 145) and before the print statements (line 147).

steps.code_spec:
Modify the stage loop (starting at line 155) to skip stages before the resume point. Inside the `for i, (name, script_name, input_key) in enumerate(STAGES, 1):` loop, add at the very top of the loop body (before `script_path = ...`):

```python
            # Skip stages before resume point
            if resume_from is not None and not reached_resume:

                    reached_resume = True
                else:

```

Also add `reached_resume = (resume_from is None)` before the loop starts (right before the `try:` block on line 154). This boolean starts True if no --resume-from (so nothing is skipped), or False if resuming (so stages are skipped until we hit the target).


Then indent the existing `original_branch`, `create_branch` try/except block (lines 273-280) under the `else:`. The full replacement block becomes:
```python
    # Remember original branch to return to on error
    original_branch = get_current_branch()

    # Check out existing branch or create new one
    if branch_exists(branch):
        print(f"Branch {branch} already exists, checking out", file=sys.stderr)
        result = git("checkout", branch)
        if result.returncode != 0:

            sys.exit(1)
```

Note: `original_branch` must be captured BEFORE the checkout/create, so move it above the if/else block. The `original_branch` assignment currently at line 273 stays in its position (before the branch logic).

steps.description: Verify implementation against all acceptance criteria
steps.code_spec:
Verify by reading both modified files and checking:

1. run.py has argparse with --resume-from flag that accepts a stage name string
2. run.py validates --resume-from against STAGES list and prints 'Unknown stage: <name>. Valid stages: validate_intake, auto_refine, auto_plan, executor, auto_harden, approval' on invalid input
3. run.py checks artifact existence before resuming and prints 'Cannot resume from <stage>: missing prerequisite artifact <path>' if missing
4. run.py's stage loop skips stages before resume_from and prints SKIPPED for each
5. run.py prints 'To resume: python pipeline/run.py <path> --resume-from <stage>' to stderr on any failure
6. executor.py checks out existing branch instead of exiting, printing 'Branch pipeline/<uuid> already exists, checking out' to stderr
7. executor.py creates new branch if it doesn't exist (unchanged behavior)
8. Normal runs (no --resume-from) work identically — resume_from is None, reached_resume is True, no stages skipped
9. --resume-from validate_intake results in all stages running (first stage is the resume point, reached_resume becomes True immediately)
10. Exit codes preserved: 0 for success, 1 for all failure cases
11. UUID path-traversal validation still runs (it's before the resume logic)
12. No new files created, no new external dependencies

Run: `python -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('pipeline/run.py').read()); ast.parse(open('pipeline/executor.py').read()); print('Syntax OK')"` to confirm both files parse correctly.

Run: `python pipeline/run.py --help` to confirm the --resume-from flag appears in help output.
